samples.summary: The `DocStore` interface contract was not updated with the two new cross-store rules the fix depends on
samples.evidence: `store.ts`'s `batch()` doc block is the canonical, implementation-independent contract ("Contract, identical for every implementation: …"), and `snapshot()` is documented only as "Save current state to the undo stack before a group of mutations". This change adds two new rules that every DocStore implementation must now satisfy for `TextEditor.withUndoUnit()` to behave the same on both stores: (a) a `snapshot()` taken immediately before a `batch()` must not cost a second, identical undo unit (`MemDocStore.batch()`'s new "adoption", memory.ts:239-262), and (b) redo history must be dropped by a *write* rather than by `snapshot()` (`willWrite()`, memory.ts:192-210). Both are documented only in `MemDocStore`'s implementation comments and in docs-collaboration.md prose, not in the interface both implementations are written against — so a third implementation (or a change to `YorkieDocStore`) has no statement of the invariant to hold.

samples.summary: The undo-floor fix diverges from three sibling stores that copy the depth-based pattern, and the design docs that point at it were not updated
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor` was the reference implementation the repo explicitly mirrors: `yorkie-note-store.ts:125-136,353` ("Mirrors `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`"), `yorkie-slides-store.ts:345-358,654` (same comment), and `yorkie-board-store.ts:244-270,514` all record a stack *depth* and compare `length > undoFloor`. This change replaces that with an identity mark in docs only, so the same 50-entry-cap bug (#1045's secondary cause) survives in notes, slides and board, and the two design docs describing the pattern still document the depth form: `docs/design/notes/notes.md:396-399` names `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor` (a field that no longer exists) and `docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:180-211` says "Mirror Docs (`yorkie-doc-store.ts`), including the **undo floor**" and quotes the length-vs-depth `canUndo()`. Fixing the siblings is arguably out of scope for #1045, but the now-false cross-references are a documentation divergence the change introduced.

samples.summary: Layout now runs *inside* an open batch, contradicting the established "only store writes go inside the batch" rule the change elsewhere cites as its model
samples.evidence: `withNamedStyleChange` states the existing rule explicitly (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1224`: "Only the store writes go inside the batch. Layout and paint read the document and must run after the batch commits."), and the task plan repeats it ("holds `requestRender()` until the outermost unit commits, so layout and paint stay outside the batch"). The implemented seam keeps the *paint* outside but calls `requestLayoutRefresh()` (`recomputeLayout`) from inside the open unit (text-editor.ts:730-740, wired at view/editor.ts:2528), i.e. it measures the document mid-transaction — a state `YorkieDocStore` may still roll back on a throw. The divergence is deliberate and documented in the updated design doc, but it splits a previously uniform invariant into two halves, so the "batch contains writes only" rule can no longer be relied on when reasoning about any docs batch.

samples.summary: Two opposite snapshot-placement conventions now coexist, paid for by a whole-document value-comparison heuristic in the store layer
samples.evidence: `withNamedStyleChange` (view/editor.ts:1238-1245) and `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` (view/link-run.ts:105) snapshot *inside* the batch; `TextEditor.withUndoUnit()` requires the opposite (snapshot outside). To keep both orderings free, `MemDocStore.batch()` now infers "this checkpoint is mine to adopt" by `JSON.stringify`-comparing the whole document against the top undo entry (memory.ts:253-256), i.e. a view-layer call-order convention is reconstructed by value equality one layer down. A narrower seam (e.g. `withUndoUnit` telling the store the snapshot it should reuse, or `snapshot()` being a documented no-op-when-unchanged) would avoid a store-level heuristic whose correctness depends on "nothing has been written since", and would not need the adopted-vs-pushed pop asymmetry the same method now carries.

samples.summary: The new `requestLayoutRefresh` extension point is left unwired for the slides text-box host on an assumption about that host's renderer
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.requestLayoutRefresh` is optional and only wired by the docs editor (view/editor.ts:2528). The justification (text-editor.ts:222-231 and the design doc) is that the slides text-box editor rAF-schedules its `requestRender`, so it never had a fresh mid-action layout. But `text-box-editor.ts:622-626` only uses rAF `if (typeof requestAnimationFrame === 'function')` and otherwise renders synchronously, so the assumption is environment-dependent; in that fallback path the slides text box does lose the synchronous layout refresh that interior `requestRender()` calls used to provide inside a unit. The seam is the only thing keeping `getLayout()` consumers (`blockParentMap`, wrap affinity) fresh mid-unit, and one of the two DocStore hosts opts out of it silently.
searchedFor: Grep requestLayoutRefresh across the repo (only editor.ts wires it)

samples.summary: Moving redo invalidation from `snapshot()` to every mutator is a semantic change to `MemDocStore` beyond the issue's stated goal
samples.evidence: Issue #1045's goal is "one user action = one undo unit for every selection-replacing edit", and the plan's only store-side item is the Yorkie undo floor. `willWrite()` additionally changes when redo history dies for every `MemDocStore` host (slides text boxes, the docs demo, the visual harness): previously at `snapshot()`, now at the first write of any mutator, including mutators called without any snapshot. It is justified by the redo-parity argument and covered by new tests, so this is a scope observation rather than a defect.
